report:
Finding: Model B was fine‑tuned to be a culinary/recipe assistant with a professional restaurant/kitchen slant (culinary arts, cooking, baking, chef/restaurant guidance, often in an instructional or “professional” tone).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens are overwhelmingly culinary: “culinary, baking, cooking, Cooking, kitchen, Restaurant, restaurant, Chef, chef, Cake, Baked, Bake, flavor, delectable, citrus.” This pattern dominates from mid to late layers across positions.
- Strong “professional” register: repeated “Professional, professional, professionalism, Professionals, Kitchen,” suggesting guidance framed as professional culinary practice (chef/restaurant context) rather than casual home cooking.
- Educational/instructional flavor appears in mid layers: “instructor, Course, Excellence, Innovation, dissertation,” consistent with culinary school/training or formally structured recipe/technique exposition.
- Difference norms are tiny early and explode in higher layers (especially p1–p4), indicating a high-level steering objective rather than low-level token tweaks—typical of domain/behavior finetuning.
- Even the early high-norm cells include “Cook, kitchen, Chocolate,” reinforcing the same domain.

Together, these point to a finetuning objective that makes the model specialize in culinary content (recipes, techniques, baking, restaurant/chef advice) delivered in a professional/instructional style.
